questions.question: By default (without OnPush), what triggers Angular's change detection?
options: Zone.js patches common async APIs (setTimeout, events, promises, HTTP) and triggers a full tree check when they fire
A timer that runs once per second
questions.explanation: Zone.js monkey-patches async browser APIs so Angular knows something might have changed, then checks the whole component tree by default.

questions.question: Under `ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush`, why doesn't mutating a property on an `@Input()` object trigger a re-render?
options: OnPush only re-checks when the @Input() reference itself changes, not when a property inside it is mutated
Mutations are automatically detected some other way
questions.explanation: OnPush skips checking a component unless the input reference changes (among a few other triggers), so mutating the object in place is invisible to it — you must replace the object.

questions.question: What is the key advantage of `computed()` over manually memoizing a derived value?
options: It automatically tracks which signals it reads and recalculates only when one of them changes
questions.explanation: computed() figures out its own dependencies at runtime — no manual dependency array needed, unlike useMemo in React.

questions.question: What direction is Angular moving toward with signals?
options: Fine-grained reactivity that can eventually run without Zone.js
questions.explanation: Signals track dependencies precisely and update only what's affected, which is why Angular now supports running zoneless for components built entirely on signals.
